title: Don't let a landed config schema change break the running Athena
summary: When a job's commit adds a new athena.toml section, the old running binary fails with "unknown field" while landing. The fix is to make the running Athena read the config of a landed commit tolerantly (fall back to its compiled-in config) instead of failing. The audience is the maintainer running Athena, who wants landing to succeed after schema-changing jobs.

defaults_applied.how: The fix targets the shared config-reading path used after landing, not the single [parallel] instance.
Adds regression tests; cargo test and clippy must pass.
Criteria run landing with an unknown-section config and check that it succeeds.
One focused change to config reading after landing.
Behavior criteria name cargo commands the verifier can run.
The CHANGELOG entry is written for an outside reader.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Root cause: athena_gate::config_at (crates/athena-gate/src/lib.rs) strictly parses the athena.toml of a landed commit, with unknown fields denied. The running binary has an older schema, and the post-landing reads at run.rs:1750 and gh.rs:1199 propagate the error with '?'.

Chosen approach is tolerate, not rebuild. Post-landing reads that need only non-gating values (model name, merge settings) fall back to the running build's config when the config parses only under a newer schema. The validity gate still rejects bad configs through the admission/content checks.
Rebuild-before-read is out of reach for a long-running process. Rebuilding would need a re-exec design, so it is recorded as the rejected alternative.

Config errors must still fail closed when the file is genuinely malformed. Only an unknown-field error caused by a newer schema is tolerated, and the tolerance applies on the landing path, not to the gate that judges new commits.
No change to athena.toml or defaults.toml is needed.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new test builds a repository whose HEAD athena.toml contains an extra unknown section, then runs the landing code path that reads the config after the commit lands (run.rs retry-landing and gh.rs). Landing completes instead of failing with 'unknown field'. Run: cargo test -p athena-core -p athena-gate.

A test shows that a genuinely malformed athena.toml (a TOML syntax error, or a wrong type for a known field) is still rejected by the gate's checks, so the tolerance does not weaken validation. Run: cargo test.
cargo test and cargo clippy --all-targets pass, and cargo fmt --check is clean.
The fix is in the shared config-reading path (config_at or a helper next to it), not patched at one call site. Every post-landing reader (run.rs, gh.rs, wiring.rs) goes through it.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry that explains the failure and the chosen tolerance, and names the rejected alternative (rebuild or re-exec before reading).

out_of_scope: Re-exec or self-rebuild of the Athena binary mid-run.
Relaxing validation of athena.toml for commits being judged by the gate.
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml, or workflows.
departures: Slightly lower acceptance than the reference. The request allows two fixes (rebuild or tolerate), and the call sites to change are uncertain.
